content: Firestore security rules scoping (firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/security/rules-conditions + transactions page): canonical per-user pattern is match /users/{userId} with allow read/update/delete: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId (doc-id keyed) or resource.data.uid == request.auth.uid (uid-field keyed, as in the project's schema). Immutable-field enforcement: compare request.resource.data.field == resource.data.field on update (e.g. isDefault immutability) — exactly the pattern in backend-schema.md. Cross-doc checks use get()/exists() (billed reads; access-call limits 10/single op, 20/batch+transaction). Server/console writes bypass rules entirely (IAM), so console seeding of the default account is legal.
